title: Claude Code's Deny Rules Silently Never Ran
caption:
Turns out a parenthesis in a path was enough to switch a deny rule off.

Claude Code 2.1.260 fixed three ways a permission rule silently never applied: a paren in the path dropped it as invalid, stray text after the closing paren matched nothing, one unclosed bracket broke every edit. Folders marked read-only stayed writable.

Config that fails open and says nothing is the part of agent tooling I trust least.

When did you last check yours?

slides.headline:
Your Deny Rules
Weren’t Running
slides.sub: Claude Code 2.1.260, out Sept 3, fixed three ways a permission rule you wrote never applied.

slides.title: Written, Then Ignored
items: A parenthesis in the path dropped the rule as invalid — the read-only folder stayed writable
Text after the closing paren, like Bash(ls) x, never matched anything and was silently ignored
One unclosed bracket made every file edit fail with Invalid regular expression

slides.title: Hidden In A Timer
slides.sub: Permission checks auto-approved zsh commands that hid a command substitution inside a REPORTTIME assignment. Now they prompt.

slides.title: Then It Broke Builds
slides.sub: 2.1.259 applied Read() deny rules to Bash arguments. Under Read(./**/build/**), npm run build was denied in every mode. Reverted.
